population: DEVELOPMENT + SYNTHETIC -- no confirmatory holdout material anywhere
contract: A39.3 (control sources) as amended by A40 (live boundary control)

tests.test: DELETE changes the NON-SPACE character sequence
tests.fails_when: deleting a word leaves the non-space sequence intact, i.e. nothing was removed

tests.test: WELD leaves non-space identical and removes exactly ONE boundary (1 -> 0)
tests.fails_when: weld changed a character, or moved more than one boundary -- it would then be a content corruption rather than the missing-boundary class M3 distinguishes

tests.test: SPLIT leaves non-space identical and inserts exactly ONE boundary (0 -> 1)
tests.fails_when: split changed a character, or moved more than one boundary

tests.test: SPLIT is the exact complement of WELD
tests.fails_when: the two classes are not complementary, so N-A no longer spans both M3 directions

tests.test: the SPLIT example matches the A40.2 illustration
tests.fails_when: the frozen floor(len/2) target produces a different string than A40.2 specifies

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- a DEAD mutation (before == after) is not live
tests.fails_when: an unchanged string is accepted as a mutation, which is exactly the A39.3 failure the size control was retired for

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- the RETIRED size variant can never be live
tests.fails_when: PULL_HEADING_TO_BODY_SIZE is still treated as a valid mutation class

tests.test: both SPLIT pieces are at least 3 characters
tests.fails_when: a split leaves a 1-2 character fragment, which is a different failure mode

tests.test: the manifest holds exactly 8 N-A, 8 N-B, 4 N-C
tests.fails_when: a control class is under- or over-populated, so a Rule 3 blocker is not satisfied

tests.test: N-A realizes the frozen 3 / 3 / 2 allocation
tests.fails_when: the index-mod-3 schedule was not applied, so the three M3 directions are not balanced as A40.1 freezes them

tests.test: every N-A mutation is LIVE on the realized fixtures
tests.fails_when: a realized control cannot fire, so it reports coverage the study does not have

tests.test: the RETIRED variant appears nowhere in the realized set
tests.fails_when: PULL_HEADING_TO_BODY_SIZE survived the A40 retirement

tests.test: every N-C expects EXACTLY no headings
tests.fails_when: a constructionally heading-free region expects a heading, so the over-triggering control could never fail

tests.test: every N-A and N-B carries paired GPO XML corroboration
tests.fails_when: a control's truth rests on something other than the independent source -- in the worst case on H or X's own output

tests.test: all 20 control identities are unique
tests.fails_when: two controls share an identity, so one would silently overwrite the other

tests.test: every generated N-A prints its mutation in the TARGET REGION exactly once
tests.fails_when: the mutation did not reach the adjudicated region, so the stimulus would not contain the alteration the control exists to test

tests.test: ...and the ORIGINAL heading is absent from that TARGET REGION
tests.fails_when: the unmutated heading survives inside the crop, so the region shows both and the control cannot distinguish an oracle that saw the alteration

tests.test: DIAGNOSTIC -- some N-A pages legitimately repeat the original heading OUTSIDE the crop
tests.fails_when: no fixture exercises the duplicate-elsewhere case, so the occurrence-scoped rule is indistinguishable from the page-scoped one it replaced

tests.test: NEGATIVE A -- an original heading INSIDE the target region is detected
tests.fails_when: an unmutated heading inside the crop goes unnoticed, so the region rule cannot fail

tests.test: NEGATIVE B -- a mutation absent from the target region is detected
tests.fails_when: the mutation counts even when it lies outside the crop, so the rule would pass a stimulus that shows the adjudicator nothing

tests.test: POSITIVE -- a fixture whose original repeats ELSEWHERE on the page still passes
tests.fails_when: the rule still gates on an unrelated duplicate outside the selected region, which is the scope error A40.13 corrects

tests.test: the four N-C controls render to FOUR DISTINCT PNG hashes
tests.fails_when: two heading-free controls are the same image, so the four-item N-C denominator is really fewer -- and container SHA uniqueness would have hidden it

tests.test: ...through the REAL build_oracle.render_region at the frozen primary DPI
tests.fails_when: the distinctness was measured by some other path than the one that will render the actual stimulus

tests.test: container SHAs are distinct too, but are NOT the evidence
tests.fails_when: the generated files are byte-identical, which is a different defect

tests.test: a clean rebuild reproduces IDENTICAL bytes for every generated fixture
tests.fails_when: a rebuild from identical inputs produces different bytes, so every committed hash goes stale on the next run and G6 cannot stay green

tests.test: the fixtures actually carry a canonicalised PDF /ID
tests.fails_when: a generated PDF has no /ID array, so the canonicalisation silently did nothing and reproducibility would depend on luck

tests.test: the authoritative holdout SHA set is non-empty
tests.fails_when: the membership manifest yielded no source hashes, so the identity guard would be vacuous and every control would pass it trivially

tests.test: no committed control carries a holdout source identity
tests.fails_when: a control's bytes are a confirmatory source

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- a DEVELOPMENT-looking record carrying a holdout SHA is REJECTED
tests.fails_when: confirmatory bytes copied in under an innocuous document id and path pass the gate, because nothing about the bytes has to change to defeat a name-based scan

tests.test: ...and the name-based scan alone would NOT have caught it
tests.fails_when: the name scan happens to catch this case, so the identity check is not what is being demonstrated and the control proves less than it claims

tests.test: the realized manifest carries NO defect except the declared-outstanding replays
tests.fails_when: either the validator rejects a correctly built fixture set, or a real defect is hiding among the outstanding-replay markers

tests.test: G6 is NOT green while its section-12 meaning is incomplete
tests.fails_when: G6 reports PASS without the independent source-selection and mutation-target replays, which is the semantic false green A40.12 exists to remove

tests.test: EVERY injected defect makes G6 FAIL with its own reason
tests.fails_when: an injected defect passes validation -- a green G6 would then certify a fixture set that cannot satisfy its Rule 3 blockers

tests.test: NEGATIVE -- changing the generated PDF BYTES with a stale manifest hash FAILS
tests.fails_when: the validator compares recorded strings rather than recomputing from the file, so a silently edited fixture would keep certifying

tests.test: ...and restoring the bytes clears the byte defect (only the outstanding replays remain)
tests.fails_when: the byte-level control left the fixture set permanently invalid
